verses.1: Having heard those words of Rama, whose deeds are unblemished, the ascetic, with his head still bowed, then spoke the following words.
verses.2: The ascetic declared that he was born in a Shudra family, named Shambuka, and that he sought to attain divinity with his physical body, O greatly renowned Rama.
verses.3: Shambuka affirmed to Rama that he was not speaking falsely out of a desire to conquer the world of gods, and asked Rama to know him as a Shudra engaged in severe penance.
verses.4: Rama, having drawn his spotless sword of very beautiful luster from its sheath, cut off the head of that Shudra while he was speaking.
verses.5: When that Shudra was killed, the gods, led by Indra and Agni, repeatedly praised Rama, exclaiming "Excellent! Excellent!"
verses.6: A great shower of divine, very fragrant flowers, released by the wind, fell down from all sides.
verses.7: The very pleased gods then said to Rama, the one of true valor, "O gentle and great-minded one, this task for the gods has been well accomplished by you."
verses.8: "O gentle one, subduer of enemies, and delight of the Raghus, accept any boon you desire, for this Shudra will certainly not attain heaven because of your action."
verses.9: Having heard the words of the gods, Rama, composed and with folded hands, spoke to Indra, the thousand-eyed destroyer of cities.
verses.10: Rama requested that if the gods were pleased with him, they should grant his greatest desire: that the brahmin's son be brought back to life.
verses.11: Rama declared that the brahmin's only son, whose time had not yet come, was taken to Yama's abode due to Rama's own transgression.
verses.12: Rama urged the gods to revive the child, wishing them well, and reminded them that he had promised the brahmin to bring his son back to life, thus he could not allow his word to be false.
verses.13: Having heard Rama's words, the best among the gods, pleased and filled with affection, replied to Rama.
verses.14: O Kakutstha, be relieved, for that boy has regained his life and is reunited with his relatives this very day.
verses.15: O Kakutstha, the very moment this Shudra was struck down, that boy was reunited with his life.
verses.16: May you obtain well-being, O best among men, and may good fortune be yours; we wish to go and see the hermitage of Agastya, O Raghava.
verses.17: The consecratory vow of that brahmin-sage of great splendour is now completed, for the twelfth year has passed as he lay abiding upon a bed of water.
verses.18: O Kakutstha, we shall therefore go to greet that sage, and you too should come, for your welfare, to see that best of sages.
verses.19: Having thus agreed to the words of the gods, Rama, the delight of the Raghus, ascended that Pushpaka aerial chariot, which was adorned with gold.
verses.20: Then, the gods departed in their vast aerial chariots, and Rama also quickly followed them to the hermitage of Agastya.
verses.21: Upon seeing the arrived gods, the righteous Agastya, a treasure-house of austerities, worshipped all of them equally without distinction.
verses.22: Having accepted the worship and honored the great sage, the delighted gods then departed to heaven with their followers.
verses.23: After the gods had departed, Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, descended from the Pushpaka chariot and then saluted Agastya, the foremost of sages.
verses.24: Having saluted the great-souled Agastya, who shone as if with brilliance, and having received excellent hospitality, the king of men, Rama, then sat down.
verses.25: The greatly effulgent and great ascetic Agastya said to him, "Welcome to you, O best among men, O scion of Raghu, fortunately you have arrived."
verses.26: O Rama, you are highly esteemed by me for your many excellent qualities, and you are a guest worthy of worship, always residing in my heart.
verses.27: Indeed, the gods speak of you as having come after slaying the Shudra (Shambuka), and by your righteous action, the Brahmin's son was brought back to life.
verses.28: O scion of Raghu, please stay here for the night near me, and in the morning, you will certainly go to your city by the Pushpaka chariot.
verses.29: Indeed, you are the glorious Narayana, in whom everything is established; you are the lord of all gods, and you are the eternal being.
verses.30: O gentle Raghava, please accept this divine ornament, created by Vishwakarma, which shines with its own splendor and divine form, and by doing so, fulfill my wish.
verses.31: It is said that giving something again, once it has been given, yields a very great reward, and indeed, you are capable of sustaining even Indra and the Maruts.
verses.32: Indeed, you are capable of protecting even the gods, including Indra, therefore I will properly give this to you; O king of men, please accept it.
verses.33: This divine and wonderful ornament shines brilliantly like the sun.
verses.34: Then, Rama, the great warrior of the Ikshvakus and the best among the intelligent, spoke to the great-souled one, remembering the duties of a Kshatriya.
verses.35: Rama questions the sage, asking how he, a Kshatriya, can accept a gift that is considered blameless only for a Brahmana.
verses.36: Rama further requested the sage to explain the reason for accepting such a gift, especially when given by a Brahmana, to which the great sage then replied.
verses.37: The great sage began by telling Rama that in the ancient Krita Yuga, when the world was pure, all people were without an earthly king, though Indra was the ruler of the gods.
verses.38: Those people approached the Lord of gods (Brahma) requesting a king, reminding him that he had already established Indra as the king of the gods.
verses.39: The people implored Brahma, the Lord of the worlds, to grant them an earthly king, a best among men, whom they could worship to cleanse their sins and under whose rule they could live, as they declared their supreme resolve not to live without a king.
verses.40: Having heard the words of the subjects, and having ascertained their excellent purpose.
verses.41: Then, Brahma, the best among gods, summoned all the protectors of the worlds, including Indra, and told them to bestow shares of their splendor.
verses.42: Then all the protectors of the worlds gave shares of their own splendor, and then Brahma sneezed, from which King Kṣupa was born.
verses.43: Brahma then endowed him (Kṣupa) with the shares of splendor from the protectors of the worlds, and then gave King Kṣupa as the ruler of those subjects.
verses.44: There, the king rules the earth with the share of Indra, and with the share of Varuna, the king nourishes his body.
verses.45: Then, he gave wealth to the people from the northern part (Kubera's domain), and with the southern part (Yama's domain), he ruled his subjects.
verses.46: O best among men, O delight of the Raghus, O lord, please accept this eastern part (Indra's domain) for my salvation; may good fortune be yours.
verses.47: Having heard that most righteous speech of the sage, Rama accepted that excellent ornament from the sage.
verses.48: Having accepted that excellent ornament, Rama then began to inquire about the origin of that radiant object.
verses.49: Rama asked, "How was this extremely wonderful, divine, and excellent form obtained by your revered self, or from where, or by whom was it taken away?"
verses.50: O greatly renowned Brahmana, I ask you out of curiosity, for you are indeed a supreme treasure of many wonders.
verses.51: When Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, spoke thus, the sage then replied, "Listen, O Rama, to what happened formerly in the Treta Yuga."
verses.52: O mighty-armed one, I saw a wonder in this beautiful forest region, which was solely concerning the power of charity. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्सप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 76 ।। Thus ends the seventy-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
